title: feat(security): an external organization role — portal users read their own identity rows and reach data only through explicit grants
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoFqCf6db2fM7iSSM3dJb5rf)_

Part of #25233 (stage 1 of the ruling of record 6355206139, letter B; stage 2 follows in its own PR).

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added

## What this does

A supplier's or customer's portal user can now be added to an organization with a new `external` role. Before this, such a user had to be a plain `member`. The member baseline's `sys_user_org_members` scope (`id in current_user.org_user_ids`) is OR-combined with any application policy. So the portal user read every employee and every other supplier's users through `GET /data/sys_user`, and better-auth's list-members and get-full-organization doors showed them too.

| Clause | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| role config | `plugin-auth` `auth-manager.ts` | better-auth registers `external` beside owner/admin/member, with an empty statement set. |
| E1 stamp | `core` `resolve-authz-context.ts` | `sys_member.role = external` in the active organization projects to the new reserved identity `org_external`. Its holder does not get the `everyone` anchor, and `countPositionHolders` agrees. The stamp is per organization, and with no active organization an external membership withholds the anchor (fail closed). There is no `sys_user` column. |
| E4 baseline | `plugin-security` | New shipped set `external_default`, bound by the `org_external` built-in position. It holds `member_default`'s own-row carve-outs without `sys_user_org_members`, plus a `sys_member` own-row policy. The plugin's additive human baseline (`[appDefault, member_default]`) is swapped for `[external_default]` on an external context. So neither an app's `isDefault` set nor an accepted package default reaches it, by either channel. It is not in `MANAGED_DENY_TARGET_SETS`, so no registry-driven read injection reaches it either. |
| E2 doors | `plugin-auth` `external-directory-door.ts` | After-hook on `/organization/list-members` and `/organization/get-full-organization`. When the caller's membership in the answered organization is `external`, it gets its own member row only (`total: 1`) and only invitations addressed to its own email. Every other caller is untouched. |
| E3 | `spec` `invitation-role-grant.ts` | `[external]: 'any'`, so the invite dialog offers it to every issuer. |
| E5 | `plugin-auth` `external-membership.ts` | A role list carrying `external` with another role is refused at write, on `sys_member` and `sys_invitation`, for every context. The refusal is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, with `invalid_value` on `role`. |
| E6 | same module | An external is never placed in the organization's business units. Refused: a `sys_business_unit_member` row, a `sys_user_position` anchored at one of that organization's units, an invitation conferring `external` with a `business_unit_id`, and a role change to `external` while a placement stands. An organization-wide position or a permission set is how an external gets access. |

Spec additions: `MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_EXTERNAL` and `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_ORG_EXTERNAL` (with metadata), in the closed vocabulary and the reserved identity names. The i18n bundles carry the `External` label (zh-CN 外部成员, ja-JP 外部メンバー, es-ES Externo). The api-surface and export-origins files are regenerated.

## Acceptance notes

The app-side acceptance (hotsrm 6366488714) is pinned on a real showcase boot in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-member-directory.dogfood.test.ts` (6/6). It boots with the showcase's own `isDefault` set wired, as `objectstack serve` does:

- **An external holder reads only its own `sys_user` and `sys_member` rows.** Two suppliers' externals each get exactly their own id from `GET /data/sys_user` and `GET /data/sys_member`. `list-members` and `get-full-organization` answer each one its own member row.
- **With a permission set granting one object, it reads that object and nothing else.** A supplier with a one-object grant reads `showcase_announcement` (200) and is refused `showcase_product` (403). The showcase's `isDefault` set opens `showcase_product` to every member. The supplier without a grant is refused both.
- **An ordinary member is unchanged.** It still sees all four users at the data door and at `list-members`, and still reads the app-default object.
- **E5 end to end.** An owner's `update-member-role` with `['external','member']` answers 400, and the stored role stays `member`.

Armed controls guard each negative case. The member really reads its peers, the app default really opens the object to members, and the fixture roles really landed.

Unit pins:

- `core` `resolve-authz-context.external-population.test.ts` (5). Four of them were red before the resolver change.
- `plugin-security` `external-population.test.ts` (11). These cover the set's shape, own-row filters, no directory scope, the structure tables closed, one grant only, no managed-deny injection, the position binding, and resolution through the service locator with an app default configured.
- `plugin-auth` `external-membership.test.ts` (16) and `external-directory-door.test.ts` (8).
- `spec` `membership-role-external.test.ts`.

Existing pins moved deliberately:

- The built-in position count goes from six to seven, and the reserved names from four to five.
- `org_external` is the one built-in identity that names a set. A delegate whose allowlist lacks `external_default` therefore meets the delegated-admin gate's 403 before the reserved-name 400. Either refusal stores nothing, and the posture test says so.
- `external_default` joins the field-withholding sets and the canonical set list.
- The delegated_admin and org_admin invite offers now include `external`.
- The closed better-auth role map and the dogfood vocabulary pin now include `external`.

Notes for review:

- **Clause-②:** reserving `org_external` refuses a new position by that name. No narrowing was measured for an existing holder. better-auth's doors refused `external` before this change, and no shipped set changed for an existing population. One case is unmeasured: a `sys_member` row written directly (not through better-auth) with the token `external` used to project to a position named `external`, and now projects to `org_external`. No such row exists in this repo's fixtures or seeds.
- **Out of scope, reported here for stage 2 or follow-up:**
  - better-auth's `list-teams` and the `teams` member of get-full-organization still check organization membership only, so an external sees the organization's team names (not rosters: `list-team-members` also requires the caller to be on that team).
  - `member_default` reads `sys_team`, `sys_sso_provider` and the OAuth resource tables with no row scope. That is not an external issue now, since externals no longer hold it.
  - The explain/describe surfaces still name `baselinePermissionSets`. This is the stage 2 explainer work.
  - Externals have no `owner_only` OWD floor yet. That belongs to the OWD seam in stage 2.

Verification: the plugin-security (4478), plugin-auth (3607) and core security (1092) suites pass after merging main. The role and identity pin tests in thirteen other packages pass. `typecheck` is clean for spec, core, plugin-security, plugin-auth, platform-objects and dogfood. All 109 derived gates were run and reconciled with `dispatch-gates --ran` (0 not measured).
